summary: Iter 27 — Multi-currency (priceEur/priceUsd) on products verified end-to-end. Backend (5/5 pytest, no Stripe payment finalized): product create persists priceEur=25/priceUsd=30 (GET confirms), Stripe checkout EUR qty=1 → charged_amount=25.0, USD qty=2 → charged_amount=60.0, fallback (no explicit EUR/USD) USD qty=1 → charged_amount=32.0. Frontend (Playwright, /api/geo mocked to US/USD): seller login OK, /vendeur/ajouter form → preview 'Europe : 25 € · USA/Canada : $30' matches spec, publish OK, list GET shows priceEur=25/priceUsd=30, edit page pre-fills EUR=25/USD=30, public product page shows $30 (no $32), cart shows $30 for qty=1 and $60 for qty=2, /commande order recap in USD uses explicit price ($30 for qty=1, no $32 fallback). Test products deleted (DELETE 200).

integration_issues.issue: After incrementing qty via '+' on /panier (cart page updates to $60), navigating to /commande shows qty=1 / $30 (badge=1). May be a stale cart snapshot on route change or my '+' button matched a non-qty control. Not blocking the multi-currency feature (the $30 shown is the explicit vendor USD price, not the $32 fallback), but worth confirming manually.

action_items: Verify manually or add data-testid on cart qty increment/decrement buttons so cart qty→checkout is deterministic; confirm /commande picks up latest cart state after /panier qty change.

stripe_router.py L92-96 correctly prioritizes explicit priceEur/priceUsd; fallback conversion (RATES_XOF) matches the 9000/28 & 9000/32 rule and is confirmed by the fallback test (32.0).
